purpose: World-map clutter (#9437, #9831): the faceted map's trees, rocks and cacti, read by MapClutter as unit-height textured prop meshes. Originally Tripo meshes baked to per-face colour (retired by #9831: the models, their normalised GLBs and the baking scripts are gone).

models.supersedes: The Tripo map rock (three faceted angular boulders, per-face colour) was replaced with the first-person stones' shape and texture so the rock is one material in both modes (#9831).
models.concept: content/scatter.sources.json, stones-1 (FLUX.2 klein seed 54, then TRELLIS.2)
models.derivation: blender -b --python scripts/stylise-mesh.py -- <source> content/game/models/map/rock.prop-mesh.json --height 1.0 --faces 1000 --texture-ref textures/scatter/stones.png --tile-metres 2.333 (unit height, as the other map models; the tile is the stones' texture, repeated at the same density relative to the shape as the 0.6 m first-person stones); read by MapClutter

models.provider: Tripo P2-20260801, triangle topology, 1200-face target (2026-10-05). Only the shape is used; the prompt that asked for faceted flat-shaded green is superseded by the texture.
models.derivation: blender -b --python scripts/stylise-mesh.py -- <source> content/game/models/map/cactus.prop-mesh.json --height 1.0 --faces 1300 --texture-ref textures/props/cactus.png --tile-metres 0.5 (Smart UV charts, smooth normals, unit height); the skin tile is drawn by scripts/generate-cactus-skin.py and graded with scripts/stylise-texture.py --size 128 --brightness 1.35 --saturation 0.75 --tile. Tripo's own atlas is a per-facet patchwork and is not used; a Z-Image skin tile was tried and abandoned when den-m5 stalled.

models.prompt: A single low-poly stylized wooden cargo sled for an expedition survival game: two long curved wooden runners turned up at the front, a slatted wooden deck, a canvas-covered bundle of supplies lashed on with rope, a short tow rope at the front, faceted flat-shaded, no ground base, no background, centered, game asset
models.derivation: blender -b --python scripts/stylise-mesh.py -- <source> content/game/models/sled.prop-mesh.json --height 0.857 --faces 1600 --texture-ref textures/props/sled.png --keep-uv <raw.png> (Tripo's UVs and all 1,502 triangles kept, smooth normals, metres: 2.4 m long), then scripts/stylise-texture.py <raw.png> content/game/textures/props/sled.png --size 512 --paint 1 --pull bark,sandstone,earth,stone,cloth --pull-strength 0.25 --saturation 0.85 --brightness 1.1 --sharpen 0.2, then reduced to 128 px, about 35 texels/m (asset-pipeline legacy/experiments/stele-place-study/pixel_reduce.py <512 px> sled.png --factor 4 --erode 1 --line-contrast 2 --colors 24 --luminance 0.44: area means without the line rule, which caught Tripo's small charts' borders; #9831 crunch rule); first-person sled (#9473, #9831), read by SledStore
models.promptNote: The prompt is kept as it was sent to Tripo. The model's surface is Tripo's own baked texture (2048 px), graded for the game, not faceted colour.
